name: State Machine
subtitle: Drive character or system behavior through state transitions
concept: State machine features emphasize the switching of characters, enemies, or game systems between distinct states. Each state has clear entry conditions, behaviors, and exit conditions, making complex behavior predictable and debuggable. It is the foundational engineering structure for AI, character control, and global flow management: menu to gameplay to results is a state machine, and an enemy’s patrol/engage/attack cycle is also a state machine. The biggest threat to state machines is state inflation—when the number of states grows, transition conditions clash and debugging becomes difficult. At that point, consider hierarchical state machines or behavior trees. A system should use a state machine only if its behavior can be decomposed into a finite set of mutually exclusive, well‑defined stages.
role: State machines manage complex behavior logic, allowing players and developers to understand "what stage we’re in and what will happen." They form the foundation of AI, character control, and process management.
significance: Mastering state machine features helps understand the State pattern, behavior trees, and event‑driven architectures. It is the essential path from simple scripts to complex systems.
problemsSolved: Decompose complex behavior into manageable states
Make character/enemy behavior predictable and scalable
Prevent logical confusion caused by multiple conditional checks
learningGoals: Master state transition conditions and callbacks
Extend complexity using hierarchical state machines or behavior trees
minimalRules: Systems/characters have a finite number of distinct states

combos.effect: Enable enemies to exhibit rhythmic attack, patrol, and hit reactions
Use state‑driven animation transitions to ensure consistency
Manage global game flow (Menu → Game → Results)

advancedWarnings: FSM becomes difficult to maintain with too many states
Conflicting transition conditions can cause deadlocks
Complex AI is recommended to migrate to behavior trees or hierarchical FSMs
